basis: Retinal dystrophy, cerebellar disease/neuropathy and pituitary-gonadal hormone deficiencies define this syndrome; hair changes are not established across the umbrella.
Developmental leukoencephalopathy; sensorineural hearing loss and persistent strabismus each occur in 30-79%, supporting hearing and ocular alignment dysfunction.
Hepatocerebral mitochondrial depletion causes liver disease and neuropathy; tiny retinal, renal and hearing denominators do not establish >=30% prevalence across this disease.
Mediastinal smooth-muscle tumor; no lung, airway, vessel or locomotor tissue origin is specified. Mediastinal soft tissue itself has no listed axis.
Lysosomal storage disease with progressive neurodegeneration; retinal degeneration and progressive visual loss affect most childhood-onset patients.
Viral infection umbrella; neurologic, pulmonary, renal and hemorrhagic organ patterns vary by virus and are not shared across the group.
Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism; olfactory dysfunction is supported by anosmia in 7/7. Individual bone abnormalities occur in 2/7, below the supplied frequency threshold.
Isolated glycerol metabolism defect, including asymptomatic adults; supplied myopathy/adrenal HPO suggests complex deletion GKD. Common lasting neurologic damage is not established.
Brittle sulfur-deficient hair and nail abnormalities define trichothiodystrophy; developmental impairment occurs in 20/20. Structural eye and heart abnormalities are occasional.
Telethonin disorders predominantly cause skeletal muscular dystrophy; cardiomyopathy is a separate subtype rather than common involvement across the group. No primary nerve disease.
Macular retinal degeneration; no other organ involvement is established.
Bony exostosis of the calcaneus; associated plantar fasciitis does not add another axis.
Myopia-associated degeneration of the macula; the neurological ancestor does not establish brain or peripheral nerve disease.
Precursor B-cell leukemia/lymphoma affects hematopoietic cells; the lymphoma designation adds the immune mechanism axis. No additional common organ damage is established.
Callosal malformation, infantile spasms and chorioretinal lacunae define it; vertebral/rib malformations and scoliosis are frequent (30-79%).
Persistent measles infection causes progressive encephalitis; direct chorioretinitis is annotated frequent (30-79%), although overt visual loss is less frequent.
Focal dystonia defined by involuntary eyelid contractions and impaired eyelid opening; neurological motor control and eyelids are the defining sites.
Enterocyte barrier dysfunction causes protein-losing enteropathy and secretory diarrhea; hypoalbuminemia and edema do not establish liver, blood or renal disease.
Combined immunodeficiency is the defining disease; no supplied evidence establishes common direct damage to another organ.
Tuberculous infection directly affects the iris, ciliary body and choroid; pulmonary involvement is not inherent to ocular tuberculosis.
Congenital neuronal migration disorder producing heterotopic cerebral gray matter.
Localized myofibroblastic tumor most commonly occupies skin or subcutis; muscle, bone and visceral sites are less common and do not establish shared involvement.
Generalized sensory-motor polyneuropathy and congenital finger extensor muscle/tendon aplasia define the syndrome; sweating abnormalities reflect autonomic dysfunction.
Benign fibrous neoplasm arising in bone, as specified by the parent concept.
Vertebral segmentation and rib abnormalities define the disorder; thoracic restriction causes ventilatory functional impairment in 44%. No metabolic defect is established.
